learningObjective: Compare symmetric and asymmetric quantization formulas, and identify why symmetric is preferred for weights but asymmetric can help for activations.

canonicalClaims.claim: Symmetric quantization (z=0) simplifies the quantized GEMM by eliminating zero-point cross-terms, at the cost of poorly fitting skewed distributions; asymmetric quantization fits skewed activation distributions better but requires extra cross-term corrections in the GEMM.
conditions: The GEMM kernel handles the chosen convention (symmetric-only vs. full asymmetric).
Rounding is consistent between quantize and dequantize.
nonImplications: Does not imply asymmetric always improves accuracy; symmetric weight distributions benefit from symmetric quantization.
Does not imply asymmetric GEMM is prohibitively slow — cuBLAS and TensorRT handle the extra bias term efficiently.

misconceptions.claim: Symmetric quantization to signed INT8 cannot represent negative values.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Signed INT8 represents [-127, 127] (symmetric convention) or [-128, 127] (full range); negatives are included.

misconceptions.claim: Unsigned asymmetric quantization to UINT8 has strictly more accuracy than signed symmetric INT8 because 256 > 255.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The level count differs by 1; per-distribution accuracy depends on how well the range fits, not the count.

misconceptions.claim: Symmetric and asymmetric quantization always produce identical dequantized results.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They differ in how they map the range; skewed distributions get different fidelity.

misconceptions.claim: The extra zero-point cross-terms in asymmetric GEMM require rewriting the GEMM kernel from scratch.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The corrections are additive bias terms that can be precomputed or absorbed into the epilogue; kernel structure is unchanged.

implementationFacts: TensorRT default: symmetric per-tensor for activations, symmetric per-channel for weights (avoids all zero-point terms).
performanceScenarios: Post-ReLU activations (all non-negative) benefit from asymmetric quantization mapping zero to 0.
Weight distributions in Transformers are approximately symmetric around zero; symmetric quantization suffices.
